name: Larry Ellison
role: American businessman, co-founder and chief technology officer of Oracle (born 1944)
summary: Ellison, Oracle's founder, speaks mostly about technology and business; his clearest political statements are for a national ID card and databases after the 2001 attacks and for constant AI-powered surveillance of police and citizens in 2024.

sources.title: CNN Moneyline with Lou Dobbs, 30 Oct 2001: Larry Ellison interview (CNN transcript, via the MediaSum corpus, CNN-42810)
sources.author: Larry Ellison

sources.author: James K. Glassman (reporting Ellison's proposal)
sources.usedFor: Ellison proposed a national ID card and offered Oracle's software for it

searched his name with the national ID card and with 2024 surveillance remarks; no other first-hand statements found

surveillance-ok.rationale: After the 2001 attacks he said 'we have to give them the tools -- databases, cards -- and the latitude to protect us' and proposed a national ID card, offering Oracle's software for it; in 2024 he told analysts 'citizens will be on their best behavior because we're constantly recording and reporting' and that Oracle would supply the AI for it.

notes: A new audit built from the few first-hand statements found: CNN and press-quoted remarks on surveillance and a national ID card (2001, 2024). Everything else he has said publicly concerns Oracle, Microsoft or technology and states no position on a bank statement, so one statement is answered and the uncertainty rule is not met.
